event.summary: Delete documentation overstates the admission timeout's decision guarantee
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 47f33bbdbd5ff4a6e437e97a800f9083be43096e. TLDR: the new Delete documentation gives maintainers a stronger deadline and no-decision guarantee than this handler implements. A future caller or test relying on it could mistake an expired reply deadline for proof that deletion cannot still occur. The established issue is internal contract documentation, not an observed late deletion or a proved false message in the shipped UI. Exact source: handlers.rs:1424-1427 says 'the waits before the decision are bounded (`SupervisorTimeouts:: seal_delete_wait`): a helm with its own deadline is waiting, and a decision taken after it gave up would contradict the "nothing was decided" it showed the user.' The inline claim at 1454-1458 begins 'Every lock this Delete waits for before deciding is inside the bound'. Actual timeout at 1459-1471 contains the agent fence, general permit, directory admission and lifecycle claim only. After it expires successfully, the decision future acquires the sessions-map mutex at 1492-1495, runs prepare_teardown at 1509-1514 and awaits seal_unless_other_sessions at 1515-1518, all outside that timeout. Preflight itself awaits host settling and then serial host-root queries at teardown.rs:492-507 and session_hosts.rs:525-537. Thus the named duration bounds admission acquisition, not every predecision lock/work item or the time of the decision. The word 'Every' is not made true by intending only the four admission locks: the map mutex is another explicit later lock in this very function. Source does not establish a global deadline even if ordinary holds are short. SPEC_impl.md:6601-6603 has parallel decision-before-helm-gives-up motivation; its parenthetical four-lock list can accurately describe those admission waits, but it must not be interpreted as a total preflight/decision bound. Fix direction: explicitly name the admission-only budget, distinguish preflight and store work, and explain that an unanswered request has an uncertain result rather than promising no later decision. If a true global decision bound is intended instead, that needs a different contract and implementation; simply cancelling a store write may not cancel its owned database operation. Original consequence preserved: l1 began as possible late sealing after false user reassurance. That shipped-user premise is refuted by the actual later endpoint caller 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db, sessions/sandbox.rs:221-239: its 240-second deadline answers 'Farhelm cannot tell whether the session was deleted'. api/sandbox_sessions.rs:218-235 preserves that reason; list/view.rs:2998-3025 either displays it or opens a new warned question without automatically widening the Delete. There is no helm sender at the recorded supervisor/protocol-phase revision. These facts refute the original runtime claim, but do not make the new internal documentation accurate. Suggested bucket: other (documentation correctness). Confidence: confirmed by source and exact comment/control-flow comparison, no runtime execution. proposed_drop: false for the documentation defect; prior proposed drop of the whole record based on absence of runtime harm is superseded, with the original runtime-route refutation retained. possible_cover: none; supplied neighbour records concern distinct comments, test oracles and lifecycle bugs. Could-be-highest: false for this established documentation defect; no security or lost-work route is established. All original conditional-confirmation limits remain: the initial Delete consent covers the last environment's processes/files/snapshots, and seal recovery after a lost reply is specified. No parent drop or lowering has been accepted. This revision resolves the parent's doc-disposition question before the fresh discovery search.

event.summary: Seal snapshot taken before listing is eventually refreshed
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 47f33bbdbd5ff4a6e437e97a800f9083be43096e. TLDR considered: a listing started before sealing could omit the seal after cleanup has already changed the session list, delaying destruction of the environment. Checks/results: handlers.rs:616 captures sealed before awaiting list_all; handlers.rs:1559-1563 stores true and hints immediately after the durable transaction, including before cleanup can fail. hints.rs:27-35 retains trailing notifications, lines 48-51 explicitly allow dropping hints to full queues because periodic polling is the backstop; lines 151-163 implement the retained Notify permit and trailing send. A stale first listing therefore does not permanently hide the seal: a subsequent listing reads the monotonic true value and returns it even on listing failure or frame overflow (handlers.rs:620-628,650-670). Contract: SPEC_impl.md Environment Delete and the seal says 'SessionList.sealed carries it on every listing, since the hello is sent once per connection'; the handler documents snapshot concurrency explicitly. Suggested bucket: other; no report proposed because this is a transient snapshot with an independent refresh path, not established incorrect final state. Confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: false-positive concern refuted by post-commit hint plus periodic poll and monotonic seal. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: false; suspected consequence was delayed resource destruction/billing, with no demonstrated data-loss or security route. Caveat: eventual propagation assumes a reachable supervisor and a completing list request, as the feature's reconnect contract requires.

event.summary: Directory-admission test observes the earlier fence, not the blocked directory wait
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 47f33bbdbd5ff4a6e437e97a800f9083be43096e. TLDR: the new regression test can get its expected remaining-session count without exercising the blocked directory-admission boundary it promises to protect. It therefore gives incomplete evidence that Delete waits for an in-flight create before deciding whether to destroy the environment. This is a test-oracle defect, not a demonstrated production sealing race. Exact test sequence at handlers.rs:12654-12687: hold working_copy_operations, dispatch Delete, wait only until agent_request_locks.claimed_for_test("s1") is true (12667-12673), plant the other row (12674), release directory admission (12675), then join and assert Deleted { remaining: 1 }. No observation of Delete attempting the directory mutex, reaching a post-admission boundary, or refusing to decide while that mutex remains held exists. The comment at 12666 says 'The outcome is the proof: deciding early would have sealed.' That only excludes deciding before the test's planted INSERT, not deciding before release of directory admission. Competing source-supported mechanism: a wrongly reordered handler can acquire the agent fence and proceed through read-only preflight before acquiring directory admission, then later take directory admission only for teardown. It can suspend in preflight, allow the test to plant the second row, and count that row before the held directory mutex is released; the identical Deleted result then passes. The observation cannot distinguish that ordering. This is a control-flow counterexample, not an executed mutation/reproduction. Concrete yield/ordering premises: claimed_for_test is merely a try_lock probe of the earlier keyed mutex (core.rs:2269-2284), not a downstream barrier. dispatch_for_test spawns via handle_control and returns tasks/rx without waiting for completion (handlers.rs:5414-5436). With the planted target's terminal None, prepare_teardown calls other_pane_roots; it first awaits store.has_session_row (teardown.rs:220-224), and store operations await independent blocking tasks (db.rs:230-244). Additional host-record filesystem/preflight work occurs before the actual seal count. Nothing in that preflight requires the test's held directory mutex except the production acquisition whose ordering this test is supposed to detect. plant commits its row directly through insert_session (handlers.rs:12060-12076; store.rs:3279-3284,3307-3310), and deliberately does not acquire working_copy_operations. The test can therefore make the expected row visible during such unrelated suspension. Current production handler is correct at 1459-1469: directory acquisition precedes lifecycle and all preflight/count work. That refutes a runtime bypass, but does not supply the missing negative test oracle. Fix direction: use a deterministic admission-attempt/worker-boundary seam that demonstrates the Delete is parked on the held directory admission, and keep the guard held through a distinguishing observation before allowing the competing row/count phase. Do not infer this boundary merely from an earlier fence being held or a final count after releasing the guard. Contract: the test's own specification at 12648-12652 says it tests waiting for directory admission; the supplied checklist requires 'Wait on the named readiness oracle for the intended boundary' and 'Assert an observable that distinguishes the competing mechanisms.' Suggested bucket: other (test validity). Could-be-highest: false for the established test-quality issue; preserve the hypothetical regression consequence (prematurely sealing over a launch) without asserting a shipped destructive route. Material caveat: the test still checks the count/result and can catch some early-count interleavings; it is not claimed to prove nothing or always pass every admission regression.
